messages:
maria: Quick sync — I've been trawling RFC feedback around service auth mental models. Want to capture the decisions + tradeoffs (API keys vs ephemeral tokens, org/project scoping, proxy delegation). TL;DR: propose capability-tagged tokens + explicit project binding as our default. Thoughts?
kevin: Sounds reasonable. Two immediate concerns: backward compat for long-lived API keys, and the impact on operator tooling (rotation, listing).
kendall: Agreed. Also need to decide proxy semantics for cross-project calls — do we keep an "operator" proxy with broad scopes or require explicit per-call delegation tokens?
sam: @maria can you sketch an example token shape so product/console folks can start on UX?
maria: Yep — sketch below. Capability tags look like small verbs so audits are clearer. Token claims (example):
```json
{
  "iss": "redwood-auth",
  "sub": "svc-A",
  "project": "proj_123",
  "scope": ["generate:finalize","embed:read"],
  "exp": 1714808133,
  "kid": "ed25519:abc..."
}
```
kevin: Nice. Tradeoffs: scoped capabilities make least-privilege practical and audits easier, but add per-request policy checks. Mitigation: runtime token signature verification + local cache of signed scope->policy mapping (TTL 5m) to avoid repeated DB hits.
kendall: For proxy delegation I'd favour ephemeral delegation tokens carrying `act_as` + shortest TTL. Operator/proxy signs a short-lived token for the downstream call instead of exposing broad operator keys. That reduces blast radius.
sam: Migration idea: accept old long-lived keys for a transition window with `legacy:true` in our internal mapping. Emit telemetry and an advisory to owners on issuance page. Plan: 6 months advisory, 9 months forced rotation.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: created INFRA-2191 to add runtime token cache + telemetry for per-scope checks — tracker.redwood/INFRA-2191 :white_check_mark:
maria: Draft decision log (proposed items):
1) Default token model = capability-tagged claims + `project` binding.
2) User-facing tokens must include explicit project (no implicit org fallback).
3) Operator proxies should issue ephemeral delegation tokens (`act_as`, TTL <= 5m) rather than reusing long-lived operator keys.
4) Migration: legacy flag for 6 months; forced rotation at 9 months; console will show migration guidance.
kevin: +1 on 1 and 2. For 3 we need an ops playbook (how to debug, how to escalate if delegation fails). Add to runbooks.
kendall: I'll write a short RFC addendum with sequence diagrams (proxy -> delegate token -> downstream). Will include error cases and fallback to a read-only fallback model. Ping me for review.
sam: I'll update the console UX so token creation modal surfaces recommended least-privilege scopes and TTL slider, plus a migration banner for legacy keys.
maria: Thanks. I've filed DECISION-1722 with the summary and next steps (will paste PR link here when I open it). Anyone object to this plan being the canonical decision?
kevin: No objections. One nit: add explicit note about telemetry events we need (token.created, token.delegated, token.legacy-used) and retention policy.
kendall: Good call — also add an approval step for operator proxy issuance (audit trail).
sam: I'll coordinate with product analytics on telemetry events.
maria: Great — closing action items: kendall writes addendum RFC, kevin/infra to scope INFRA-2191, sam updates console mockups, I'll add the DECISION-1722 entry and follow up PR. Will loop back in ~1 week. :thumbsup:
